title: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel NCCL overlap, KV cache sharding, and continuous batching
author: Anya Patel
description: Context: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads at high concurrency were observing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and device compute leading to lower throughput and higher p99 latency for long sequences. This PR implements three coordinated changes to improve overlap and end-to-end throughput: 1) deterministic NCCL stream selection and prioritized stream scheduling to avoid unnecessary stream synchronization, 2) asynchronous collective invocation path and lightweight progress hooks to allow kernel work to proceed while collectives are in flight, and 3) KV cache sharding and continuous-batching-aware cache lookup path to reduce synchronization points and balance memory/comm across TP ranks. Changes are gated behind runtime flags and additive fallbacks so behavior is opt-in for early rollouts. Summary of changes: refactor of nccl_scheduler to select prioritized streams per-collective type and rank affinity; introduce async_collective APIs with small progress callback inserted into token-generation loop; add kernel_fusion for small reduction kernels to reduce kernel-launch overhead on short sequences; implement kv_cache_sharding that shards prefix cache across TP ranks and updates consistent hashing to maintain routing under model sharding; modify continuous batching scheduler to aggregate prefix-compatible requests across ranks and avoid global synchronization on batch flush; add unit and integration tests and perf harness for TP scenarios. Benchmarks: internal perf runs on 8xA100-80GB, Llama-2-13B TP4 pipeline: throughput +12% for steady-state generation at seq=1024, p50 latency unchanged, p99 latency reduced by 18% under 95th percentile load; memory usage per rank reduced ~6% due to sharded KV cache for long prefixes. Backwards-compatibility: default behavior unchanged; features behind flags runtime.enable_async_collectives=true and runtime.kv_cache_sharding=auto. Rollout plan: stage behind feature flag, enable on Dedicated canaries, monitor p95/p99 latency, token-cost, and NCCL error metrics; full rollout after 2 weeks of stable telemetry. Rollback: revert flags or revert merge if critical regressions observed. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests (tp/intra-node) - [x] perf harness validated - [x] docs for runtime flags - [x] internal canary run - [x] reviewers approved. Related linear issues and discussion included in linked_linear.

Add async_collective APIs and progress hooks in tp runtime loop: runtime/tensor_parallel/tp_runtime.cc, token_loop.cc
Implement KV cache sharding and lookup path: runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_shard.{cc,h}
Kernel fusion for small reductions and micro-optimizations: runtime/kernel/kernel_fusion.cc
Continuous batching scheduler updates to avoid global flush sync: runtime/batching/batching_scheduler.cc
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Please ensure NCCL stream priorities are only enabled when the driver supports cudaStreamAttrPriorityCreate to avoid ABI surprises. Author reply: Checked and guarded with runtime flag and driver capability probe.

Liam O'Connor: Can we add a smoke test that simulates KV cache skew to validate routing stability under shard rebalances? Author reply: Added tests/tp/integration/test_kv_cache_shard_rebalance.py and included in integration CI.

Priya Reddy: p99 improvements look good, but please add tracing spans for async_collective start/complete to help SRE debug overlap issues. Author reply: Added tracing spans and updated observability-pack to include span names 'async_collective.start' and 'async_collective.end'.
merge_commit_message: squash: optimize NCCL stream scheduling and KV cache sharding to improve TP overlap and continuous batching
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance: prioritized NCCL stream scheduling and async collectives to increase compute/comm overlap; KV cache sharding reduces per-rank memory and smooths comm patterns; continuous batching updates reduce global synchronization and improve throughput for mixed-prefix workloads; all changes are behind runtime flags and disabled by default.
